source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Nashville - Brentwood publishes 1.49 MW of IT capacity across 19,150 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 1.49 MW supports roughly 37 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, it supports roughly 149 racks. The arithmetic is an assumption, not an operator claim. A campus at this scale is sized for enterprise colocation rather than hyperscale AI training runs, which typically begin in the tens of megawatts.

The certifications tell a clear story about intended workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify the campus for audited financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA and HITRUST qualify it for regulated healthcare data. ISO 27001 and SSAE 18 qualify it for organizations requiring internationally recognized information security management and formal attestation standards. The full stack points toward compliance-heavy enterprise tenants, not GPU cluster operators.

Tennessee has 24 facilities mapped in this site's data, of which only 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 12.13 MW across those four. Brentwood ranks third among those four by published IT capacity. The state's aggregate published figure is modest, and most mapped facilities in Tennessee publish no capacity number at all, so the true scale of the state's data center market is not determinable from this site's data alone. This campus contributes 1.49 of the 12.13 published megawatts in the state, roughly 12 percent of what is known, which is a meaningful local share but not a figure that registers at the scale AI infrastructure planning requires.
